finding.claim: Verified tokens without an iat claim are cached with a TTL of cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) instead of their exp, so an expired token is accepted on cache hit until the cache max expires.
finding.source: Validly signed token whose payload has exp but no numeric iat (signer with noTimestamp:true and expiresIn, src/signer.js:96-102).
finding.sink: Cache-hit return of the cached payload without re-checking exp (src/verifier.js:368-378, returned at :377).

trace.note: createCache builds an LRU cache only when the cache option is set; off by default.
cacheTTL defaults to 600000 ms.
Validator loop checks exp at verification time; token is valid at time T.
cacheSet gates the exp-based TTL on hasIat; with no iat the exp branch is skipped.
Cache max is set to T + cacheTTL instead of exp.
Cache-hit check tests only min and max, never exp.
Cached payload returned for a token whose exp has passed.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified before caching; cache disabled by default; requiredClaims (src/verifier.js:293-299) mitigates only if the app requires iat; no exp re-check on cache hit.

finding.claim: maxAge is silently not enforced for tokens without an iat claim, so such tokens never expire under maxAge.
finding.source: Validly signed token with no iat claim (signer with noTimestamp:true).
finding.sink: maxAge expiry check, registered at src/verifier.js:642-644 and skipped at src/verifier.js:311-313.

trace.note: maxAge configured: an iat validator is pushed with modifier maxAge.
Loop skips any validator whose claim is absent from the payload.
requiredClaims is the only mechanism that rejects a missing iat; nothing in the library rejects a maxAge config when iat is absent.

finding.guards_checked: Signature still required; exp validator still applies if exp is present; requiredClaims including iat would block the case; no library-level rejection.

finding.claim: Signature segment is not canonical: non-zero trailing bits in the final base64url character are ignored, so one signature has several token strings that verify, despite the code comment saying the signature is canonical.
finding.source: Token holder edits the final character of the signature segment of a validly signed token.
finding.sink: Signature acceptance (verifySignature, src/crypto.js:387-391) and any application logic keyed on the raw token string (replay, revocation, single-use).

trace.note: Only charset is validated (BASE64URL_RE); no length or canonical-encoding check.
Comment asserts the signature is canonical after the charset check; this is incorrect.
verifySignature called with the raw signature string.
Buffer.from(signature, 'base64') decodes the variant to the same bytes, ignoring unused trailing bits.
timingSafeEqual over decoded bytes matches; token accepted under a different string.

finding.guards_checked: Base64url charset validation (src/decoder.js:10, :41); no length or canonical-encoding check; ECDSA low-S malleability is also unchecked (src/crypto.js:411). Claims and forgery are unaffected. Node trailing-bit behavior should be confirmed by test.

finding.claim: Public key material with no PEM header (or an explicit HS-only algorithm list with a PEM public key) is accepted as an HMAC secret, so anyone who knows the public key can forge HS tokens. Fail-open configuration path.
finding.source: Operator-supplied public key without a -----BEGIN header (for example a bare base64 body), or a PEM public key with algorithms set to HS-only.
finding.sink: HMAC verification keyed with public key bytes (secret prepared at src/verifier.js:550).

trace.note: createVerifier calls detectPublicKeyAlgorithms on the supplied key.
With an all-HS algorithm list, detection is skipped and the key is treated as a raw secret.
locatePem finds no PEM header and returns isRawSecret true.
assertNotAsymmetricJwkJson only refuses JSON-shaped JWK/JWKS; a bare base64 body passes.
Returns hsAlgorithms for the raw key.
hsAlgorithms.includes(...) is true, so the public key is prepared as a secret (createSecretKey).

finding.guards_checked: JWK/JWKS refusal (src/crypto.js:85-115, :136-140) covers JSON only; HS-vs-RS KeyObject confusion blocked because createHmac on an asymmetric KeyObject throws and is caught (src/crypto.js:389-392); precondition is operator misconfiguration and legitimate RS/ES tokens would fail, so it likely surfaces. Lowercase PEM header behavior not verified.
